analysis.investment_thesis: Aavas Financiers is among the better-quality businesses in this group — seven consecutive years of growing profits at a 29.7% CAGR serving an underserved rural housing segment — but Mr. Market prices it at P/E 21.8x and P/B 2.28x, offering no margin of safety whatsoever. The Graham Number approximates INR 946 versus a market price of INR 1,348, a 42% premium that leaves the disciplined buyer on the sidelines.
key_strengths: Unbroken net profit growth for 7 years (INR 93 Cr → INR 574 Cr, 29.7% CAGR) — the clearest indicator of durable earning power
High FII ownership (24.72%) and DII ownership (14.30%) reflect institutional validation of business quality
Focus on semi-urban and rural India — an underserved, large addressable market with lower competition from large banks
key_risks: Debt/Equity of 3.08x — the highest leverage in this group — amplifies risk if the Indian credit cycle turns
Cash on balance sheet of just INR 11 Cr against INR 13,918 Cr of debt provides virtually no liquidity buffer
P/B of 2.28x means investors pay INR 2.28 per rupee of net assets; any asset quality deterioration would be doubly painful
red_flags: Price of INR 1,348 is 42% above the estimated Graham Number of ~INR 946 — insufficient margin of safety
Operating cash flow negative in all 5 of the last 5 years, an inevitable feature of the HFC model but a permanent reminder that reported profits are not cash profits
Finance cost data anomaly in FY2025 (INR 5 Cr vs INR 828 Cr in FY2024) warrants scrutiny for reclassification or accounting changes
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Of the two housing finance companies in this group, Aavas Financiers presents the cleaner earnings trajectory and arguably the stronger franchise in the rural/semi-urban niche. However, my method is not to buy good businesses — it is to buy good businesses at prices that protect me against error and adversity. At P/E 21.8x and P/B 2.28x, there is no such protection here. The estimated Graham Number of INR 946 tells me the market is asking me to pay a 42% premium for the privilege of owning this company.

I also note with concern that the company carries INR 13,918 Cr of debt against INR 4,361 Cr of equity and only INR 11 Cr of cash. Leverage at 3.08x D/E is the fuel that amplifies both gains and losses. If India's real estate credit quality were to deteriorate — as it periodically does — this company would face stress. The intelligent investor waits for the price to come to him. At below INR 950, this becomes a conversation worth having. At INR 1,348, it does not.
